items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Also Norman Thronton and Lem Johnson was the tenor man.

ctx.x: I never knew how Archey made out with the "Beach Combers" act because I was never there until the last of the final act was being played. But Archey didn't stay in Leon's band very long and when he left, two trumpet players were engaged. They were Russell Gillon and his buddy Reese. They were both nice young fellows and both play-boys, so it was possible that Leon had hired Russel and he in turn had arranged to divide the salary in order to be together. Otherwise, why had Leon not hired another trumpet to help me…

In August I was contacted to do a two-weeks tour with Claude Hopkins, the pianist who had been quite a popular bandleader at the Savoy and the Arcadia ballrooms. Claude had no regular orchestra now and most of the musicians were engaged at the Rhythmn Club. Those that I remember on the tour were Ernest "Bass" Hill, Joe Jordon known as Pokey Joe on trumpet. Joe loved to play poker and that's how he became known as Pokey Joe. Joe Hayman was on alto. Also Norman Thronton and Lem Johnson was the tenor man. Lem was…

The most amusing thing about the tour was that Claude had engaged a small bus that could carry about 20 people. It was large enough for us because we were about 14 including the girl vocalist. Everytime we came to a hill that mounted for a quarter of a mile or more, the damn bus couldn't make it and we all had to go out and push it. Sometimes we had to stop pushing for ten minutes to get our breaths and Pokey Joe always had a pair of dice with him so the guys would take their minds off of pushing the bus and shot…
